title: Guide - Grief and Comfort - One small step

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, slow and unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Grief and Comfort. <short pause> This practice is called One Small Step. <short pause> It isn't a step away from the one you lost. <short pause> You will never be asked for that here. <short pause> It is only a step that you and your love can take together.

parts.style: tender, intimate, very soft, speaking slowly
parts.text: Feel the ground beneath you, or whatever is holding you up. <short pause> Press down very lightly, with a heel or a hand... <short pause> and let it go. <short pause> That is how small we mean. <short pause> Nothing today needs to be any bigger than that.

Grief can make us wander. <short pause> We walk into a room and forget why. <short pause> We drive the old way without thinking. <short pause> We pick things up and put them down. <short pause> It can feel like going in circles, and getting nowhere at all. <short pause> And it's easy to believe that no one is keeping track of any of it.

David knew what it was to wander. <short pause> He was running for his life, far from home, frightened and alone among strangers. <short pause> And in that place he said something astonishing about God. <short pause> It is written in Psalm fifty-six, verse eight.

parts.style: reverent, very slow, reading scripture aloud
parts.text: Thou tellest my wanderings: put thou my tears into thy bottle: are they not in thy book?

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: To tell, in that old English, can mean to count. <short pause> God counts the wanderings. <short pause> Every circle around the kitchen. <short pause> Every walk that went nowhere. <short pause> And the tears... He gathers them, the way a traveler saves water in dry country. <short pause> Not one step of this has been wasted on Him. <short pause> Not one tear has fallen unrecorded.

So you don't have to take a step in order to be seen. <short pause> You are seen already. <short pause> But love often longs for somewhere to go, when the person it belonged to is gone. <short pause> And sometimes it helps to give it one small, kind thing to do.

parts.style: gently wondering, slow, leaving room to answer
parts.text: I'll offer a few, and you can leave every one of them, if it's too soon. <short pause> You might light a candle, and say their name. <short pause> You might write them one line, beginning, I wanted to tell you. <short pause> You might tell someone a story about them. <short pause> Cook the thing they liked. <short pause> Or do one kindness that they would have done. <short pause> Is there one that your heart doesn't turn away from?

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: If one has come to you, hold it loosely. <short pause> Picture the first moment of it... the match, the pen, the name in your mouth. <short pause> If it makes you cry, that doesn't mean it was the wrong step. <short pause> Now offer it to God, just as small as it is. <short pause> Lord, here is my love. <short pause> Show it where to go.

parts.style: tender reassurance, very slow, resting between sentences
parts.text: And if today's step is only to get through today, He counts that one too. <short pause> But if getting through starts to feel impossible, or you think of harming yourself, please reach for someone now. <short pause> Your local emergency number. <short pause> A crisis line. <short pause> A person who can come and be with you. <short pause> Asking for help is a step... <short pause> and it is a brave one.

Let's pray. <short pause> God who counts my wanderings, <short pause> thank You for keeping what I have cried, and where I have been. <short pause> I don't know how to live all the days that are ahead. <short pause> So give me this one. <short pause> Bless the small step I take in love. <short pause> Walk slowly with me, for I am slow. <short pause> And keep us all in Your care, the living and those we miss, until every tear is wiped away. <short pause> Amen.

parts.style: soft, very slow blessing, resting between phrases
parts.text: Go as slowly as you like. <short pause> You can carry them with you, and still take a step. <short pause> And wherever your feet wander next... <short pause> it will be counted, and it will be kept, by the God who loves you.
